name: Serbia

facts.religion: Serbian Orthodox about 82%, Catholic and Muslim minorities

snapshot: Facing student-led protests, Aleksandar Vučić resigned the presidency in September 2026 to run for prime minister in a snap election on 25 October.
culture: Serbian Orthodox monasteries, the Cyrillic and Latin alphabets used side by side, and slava, the family patron saint's day, define Serbian tradition. Belgrade's nightlife is famous, as are its kafanas, taverns with live folk music. Novak Đoković is a national hero. Guča's trumpet festival draws hundreds of thousands.
society: Serbia balances between the EU, which it hopes to join, and Russia and China, which back it on Kosovo and invest in its economy. The 2024 collapse of a railway station canopy in Novi Sad, which killed 16 people, set off the biggest protest movement in decades, led by students. Media freedom has declined under Vučić.

story: On 1 November 2024, a newly renovated concrete canopy at the railway station in Novi Sad collapsed, killing 16 people. Serbians saw it as the product of a corrupt state that cut corners on public works, and students launched protests that grew into the largest movement against Aleksandar Vučić in his more than a decade in power. Nearly two years on, they forced him into an early election.

Vučić dissolved parliament on 9 September and called a snap election for 25 October. On 27 September, seven months before his second and final presidential term was due to end, he resigned the presidency so he can become prime minister if his Serbian Progressive Party wins (Reuters via The Print). It is a familiar manoeuvre for leaders facing term limits. His ally Ana Brnabić, the parliament speaker, is acting president, and a presidential election must be held by the end of the year. The main challengers are Students Win, the anti-corruption movement born from the protests, and European Serbia, an alliance of pro-Western parties. Vučić told CNN he would congratulate the opposition the same evening if it won, but one Serbian analyst told Al Jazeera she feared "the crisis could only begin after the October 25 elections" (Al Jazeera). Serbia balances between the EU, which it wants to join, and Russia and China, which it courts.
briefing.power: A parliamentary republic. The prime minister leads the government with the support of the 250-seat National Assembly, elected by proportional representation; the president is directly elected for up to two five-year terms. Under Vučić the presidency became the real centre of power, which may now shift with him.
briefing.holders: Aleksandar Vučić (SNS), seeking the premiership; Acting President Ana Brnabić.
